title: [review] project-LICHEN-6mij.2.4: authorize_mutating passes plain_buf to unprotect even when NULL
description:
The doc comment for coap_oscore_authorize_mutating says 'plain_buf: Buffer for decrypted payload (may be NULL if no payload expected, e.g. DELETE)'. However, the implementation always passes plain_buf at line 285 to coap_oscore_unprotect_request, which dereferences it as uint8_t* payload in its function signature (with _Nonnull annotation actually). coap_oscore_unprotect_request passes this to memcpy (unprotect path) and/or writes to it.

If coap_oscore_authorize_mutating were ever called with plain_buf=NULL and an OSCORE-protected request with a payload, coap_oscore_unprotect_request would crash writing to NULL.

Fix: Either:
1. Remove the 'may be NULL' claim from the doc and require non-NULL always (simplest, matches actual behavior)
2. Guard the unprotect call: only call coap_oscore_unprotect_request if plain_buf != NULL and plain_buf_len > 0

Affected file: lichen/subsys/lichen/oscore/coap_oscore.c lines 242-309, and the header doc at coap_oscore.h lines 156-162.
